claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has hierarchical dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Coarse internal boundaries in the untreated alloy permit long dislocation pile-ups.
Rapid directional or rapid solidification will reduce lamellar thickness.
Rapid directional or rapid solidification will produce a more uniformly distributed colony arrangement.
The resulting refined lamellar architecture will interrupt long, continuous dislocation channels.
Reducing lamellar thickness and improving colony arrangement will shorten dislocation accumulation paths at internal boundaries.
Shorter dislocation accumulation paths will limit local stress concentrations.
Limiting local stress concentrations will reduce microcracking and premature catastrophic failure.
A higher density of phase boundaries may provide additional back-stress strengthening.
The processed alloy will have significantly higher room-temperature tensile ductility than the untreated alloy.
The processed alloy will retain or slightly increase its yield strength and ultimate tensile strength.
Cryo-rolling and annealing of an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy produced a hierarchical microstructure with simultaneously enhanced strength and ductility.
The proposed improvements are anticipated under room-temperature tensile loading.
Performance at other temperatures or under extended cyclic loading is unknown.
The magnitude of the ductility improvement and the optimal target lamellar thickness are uncertain.

The hypothesis is falsified if refinement fails to produce a statistically significant ductility increase and microcrack reduction while retaining or enhancing strength relative to a conventionally processed control.
